results.title: Count estimate - PostgreSQL wiki
results.snippet: This can be rather slow because ... might be good enough and is much faster to retrieve for big tables. SELECT reltuples AS estimate FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'table_name'; estimate ----------- 100...

results.title: sql - Fast way to discover the row count of a table in PostgreSQL - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: CopySELECT reltuples::bigint AS estimate FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'myschema.mytable'::regclass;

results.title: Faster PostgreSQL Counting - Citus Data
results.snippet: We can multiply the average rows per page by up-to-date information about the current number of pages occupied by a table for a more accurate estimation of the current number of rows. -- pg_relation_size and block size have fresh info so combine them with -- the estimation of tuples per page SELECT (reltuples/relpages) * ( pg_relation_size('items') / (current_setting('block_size')::integer) ) FROM pg_class where relname = 'items'; Copy

results.title: How to get approximate row count in postgres tables? · Manoj Awasthi
results.snippet: SAMPLEDB=> SELECT reltuples::BIGINT AS estimate FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'SAMPLE'; estimate ---------- 54296044 (1 row) Ref: https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/Count_estimate
